newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Germany's BHW targets billion marks for IPO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Germany's BHW targets billion marks for IPO.

text.p: German savings bank BHW, Holding AG, traditionally a favourite of the country's civil servants, said on Thursday it is targeting a stock exchange listing of well over a billion marks ($610 million) in its IPO -- Germany's first in 1997.
BHW said it plans to put 30 percent of its 900 million marks in equity on the market in April or May and expected a capital increase of around 135 million marks.
"Coming to market will help BHW with future investments, which will help the group exploit new market opportunities," said BHW's management board chairman Reinhard Wagner.

The savings bank is the first IPO to be announced in Germany for 1997, although the German government has signalled its intention to privatise the rest of Deutsche Lufthansa airline towards the end of the year.
In terms of IPO volumes, 1997 is unlikely to outdo last year, when the first 20-million-mark tranche of the telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom was sold.
BHW said that it planned to issue a so-called "greenshoe" option, or over-allotment of extra shares, when it comes to market.
BHW is a prime candidate for a listing on the MDAX index, which measures trade in small-to-medium sized companies, the group said.
Referring to its results for 1996, BHW said its group net profits for full-year 1996 were up 20 percent from 151.2 million marks in 1995.
BHW's building society savings were up grew 16.8 percent to 17.6 billion marks, while its construction finance business grew 33.6 percent to 8.5 billion marks in 1996 in the period.

The group's planned cooperation with the post office bank Deutsche Postbank AG can begin at any time, Wagner told journalists, adding that he hoped the co-operation would officially start in the first half of the year.

The reason the planned cooperation had not yet taken place was that there had been no political decision on the issue as yet. The German federal government, which currently owns the Postbank, had yet to agree on details of the agreement.
Postbank is due to be privatised in the near future, but has been tangled in a battle with the postal service Deutsche Post AG over the ownership structure.
In November BHW and Postbank agreed on a mutual capital holding of at least ten percent in each company.
Wagner said that the planned placement on the bourse of 30 percent of the bank's base capital would take place without any recourse to the Postbank cooperation.
Wagner also said that BHW planned to purchase more shares in the bank Allgemeine Hypothekenbank (AHB) and hoped to take over management control of AHB this year.
After the IPO, the shares will be listed on the bourse in Frankfurt, as well as BHW's local bourse in Hannover.
The issue will be sponsored by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB). BHW Salomon Brothers, DG Bank and NordLB will act as co-managers.
